title: Indian American Leaders Press MEA Secretary on Passports, Property Fraud in New York
excerpt: In the first meeting of its kind, Secretary (CPV & OIA) Sripriya Ranganathan's US outreach tour reached New York, where diaspora leaders raised passport renewal hassles, VFS service gaps and grabbed NRI land back home.
body:
• Four Indian-American community leaders held a detailed meeting with Sripriya Ranganathan, Secretary (CPV & OIA) at the Ministry of External Affairs, during her first-ever multi-city US outreach tour, with Consul General Binaya Srikanta Pradhan also present in New York.
  • The leaders raised concrete grievances: inconsistent passport renewal procedures, poor VFS and consular services, unauthorized middlemen exploiting applicants, NRI properties illegally grabbed in India, misuse of legal provisions against NRIs, and the need for round-the-clock emergency consular help.
  • On grabbed NRI land, Bhandari proposed fast-track courts and administrative mechanisms for property disputes, video conferencing for hearings, and a national-level NRI coordination body.
  • The delegation also shared experience-based suggestions for the forthcoming Pravasi Bharatiya Divas, drawing on Federation of Indian Associations chairman Ankur Vaidya's attendance at 16 of the 18 PBD conventions to date.

A First for MEA Outreach

Prem Bhandari (chairman of Jaipur Foot USA), Ankur Vaidya (chairman of the Federation of Indian Associations, NY-NJ-CT-NE), Ajay Patel (president of BRUHUD New York Seniors) and Alok Kumar (trustee of the FIA) met Sripriya Ranganathan, Secretary for Consular, Passport, Visa and Overseas Indian Affairs, in a separate and detailed session in New York. Binaya Srikanta Pradhan, India's Consul General in New York, was also present.

According to a press release issued on October 2, the meeting was part of Ranganathan's extensive US outreach covering New York, Texas, San Francisco and Seattle — a tour aimed at hearing diaspora concerns directly and seeking suggestions for the forthcoming Pravasi Bharatiya Divas.

"I have been in the United States for nearly four decades, and this is the first time I have seen a Secretary (CPV & OIA) undertake such an extensive outreach in the United States to personally understand the problems and concerns of the Indian diaspora."

— Prem Bhandari, Chairman, Jaipur Foot USA

The Grievances on the Table

Bhandari put a series of bread-and-butter issues on the record. Passport renewal and re-issue procedures need simplification and, critically, consistency. VFS centres and consular services need improvement. Unauthorized agents and middlemen continue to exploit applicants. And in India, NRI properties and land are being illegally grabbed — Bhandari suggested fast-track mechanisms and courts for NRI property disputes, the use of video conferencing for court and administrative hearings, and a national-level coordination mechanism for NRI matters.

The delegation also flagged false FIRs and the misuse of legal provisions against NRIs, and pushed for stronger 24/7 emergency consular assistance.

Pravasi Bharatiya Divas on the Agenda

Vaidya, who has attended 16 of the 18 PBD conventions held so far, shared experience-based suggestions to strengthen diaspora participation and make the forthcoming edition more meaningful. Recent government initiatives — the e-OCI system, chip-enabled passports and Fast Track Immigration — were also highlighted during the discussion.

The MEA has not yet issued its own statement on the meeting, and no direct quote from Ranganathan was published in the release. The story so far is essentially an ANI wire replicated across outlets — but the community reaction itself is the news: after four decades in the US, Bhandari called the access and willingness to listen unprecedented.

Diaspora Angle

For Indian-Americans, the significance lies less in the specific promises — none were detailed — and more in the format. The ministry's diaspora chief touring American cities with a listening brief, taking notes on passport counters and grabbed ancestral land, is a departure from the usual ceremonial diaspora engagement. Whether the grievances turn into policy will be the measure to watch at the next Pravasi Bharatiya Divas.
image_caption: Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri, who was pressed by Indian American leaders on passports and property fraud issues

author: Diaspora Desk
